title: Pskov Republic
capsule: The Pskov Republic was a self-governing city-state in northwestern Russia, formally recognized as independent from Novgorod by the Treaty of Bolotovo in 1348, though it had exercised substantial autonomy earlier. Its institutions centered on a veche (popular assembly), an elected posadnik (mayor), and a resident prince whose powers were strictly circumscribed by civic charter; the Pskov Judicial Charter of 1397 codified commercial, criminal, and inheritance law and stands as one of the most sophisticated medieval Russian legal texts. Strategically positioned between Livonia, Lithuania, and Muscovy, Pskov maintained a mercantile economy trading furs and linen westward through Riga and Reval. Grand Prince Vasily III of Moscow absorbed the republic in 1510, removing the veche bell and deporting roughly 300 prominent families to central Russia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's territorial extent is reasonably documented through Livonian and Russian sources, though the precise border with Novgorodian and Lithuanian territories at different periods remains subject to scholarly debate.
